newsitem.title: USA: Trinova buys aerospace industry parts maker.
newsitem.headline: Trinova buys aerospace industry parts maker.

text.p: Trinova said Tuesday that its Vickers unit has agreed to buy the Electrical Engineering & Manufacturing Co from privately-held Datron Inc for about $35 million.
Trinova said the aerospace parts maker has annual sales of about $37 million and that the purchase should close by year end.
Trinova said its strategy calls for aerospace sales to grow to more than $600 million in the year 2000, up from $339 million.

"Based upon programs and expected production levels -- plus sales of new products, acquisitions and new markets -- we feel confident that our growth scenario conservatively reflects our aerospace potential," the company said in a release.

Trinova is the parent of Aeroquip Corp and Vickers Inc, two companies that make engineered components and systems for the aerospace, automotive and industrial markets. Vickers makes mostly hydraulic and electric components, said spokesman Peter Parsons.
